Adv.P.K.Manojkumar
 This Motor Accident Claims Appeal Having Come Up For
Hearing On 07.08.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered
The Following:
 M.A.C.A.No.434 of 2020

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.315/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mavelikkara (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 28/06/2019.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 11/11/2008 while he was riding his bicycle through Thrikkunnappuzha - Karthikappally road, motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-29A-4480 ridden Gireesh @ Giri vs Achu (Driver) on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147096723/
2 by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner and in high speed knocked him down,
2025:KER:59088 as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/rider and the second respondent-owner of the offending motorcycle remained ex-parte.
4. The third respondent-insurer filed written statement admitting the policy, but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent.

The averments in the petition regarding age, academic status,
occupation and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A15 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent-rider of the offending motorcycle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 1,75,800/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with 2025:KER:59088 proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides.
9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter was working as a helper to mason earning 15,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 4,000/- only, which is on the lower side and hence the same needs to be appropriately enhanced.
There are no materials on record to substantiate the claim regarding the monthly earnings of the claim petitioner.

However, going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236, the notional 2025:KER:59088 income can be fixed at 6,500/- per month.

sentences.text: Loss of amenities and compensation for deformity.
10. An amount of 6,00,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 25,000/-.
This is stated to be on the lower side.

However, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the accident took place in the year 2008 and therefore an amount of 25,000/- awarded under this head is quite just and reasonable and that it does not call for any interference.

Ext.A12 certificate reads- "Certificate This is to certify that Mr. Gireesh kumar 36 years, whose signature is given below IP No 36015 was refered from Alapuzha following an RTA and admitted Gireesh @ Giri vs Achu (Driver) on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147096723/
3

at MCH Kottayam on 11/11/2008 with history of alleged RTA and head injury Verified the records and discharge summary CT Scan showed(26/04/2008)- Lt frontal contusion, fracture frontal bone, nasal bone, orbit, zygoma, pneumocepalus,
Minimal SAH.

Comminuted fracture anteriori wall of b/l maxillary sinus, Rt zygoma,
frontal bone, nasal bones and both orbits.
He was taken up for surgery after stabilization of vitals Left frontal craniotomy and decompression done.
He was on close monitoring and he improved in his clinical status.
He was discharged on 29.11.2008.
He is still on treatment with medications on an OP basis and requires prolonged anticonvulsive treatment.

Patient now has 1. Bilateral anosmia 3%
2. Emotional disturbances and occasional memory loss- 9%
3. Requires antiepileptic drugs for prolonged period - 3%
Total permanent disability -(TEN)------ 15%"
Hence, taking into account the injuries and the resultant disabilities, I find that an amount of 30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Percentage of disability 11.
As per Exhibit A12 certificate, the percentage of disability assessed is 15%.

The Tribunal fixed the functional disability at 10%, which is submitted to be wrong in the light of the disability sustained,
which includes anosmia.
I have already referred to the contents in Ext.A12 and the findings.

In the light of the avocation of the claim petitioner and taking into account the injuries and disability sustained, I find that the functional disability of 10% fixed by the Tribunal is reasonable and that it does not ca ll for any interference.
12.

The impugned Award is modified to the following extent:
Sl. Head of claim Amount Amount Modified in No. claimed Awarded appeal by Tribunal (in ) (in ) (in )
1. Loss of earnings Nil Nil Nil 2. Partial loss of Nil Nil Nil earnings

3. Transport to 20,000/- 4,000/- 4,000/-

4  hospital (No modification)
4. Extra nourishment 25,000/- 3,000/- 3,000/-
 (No modification)
5. Damage to 1,500/- 1,000/- 1,000/-
 clothing (No modification)
6. Medical expenses 1,00,000/- 18,000/- 18,000/-
 (No modification)
7. Bystander's 72,000/- 4,000/- 4,000/-
 expenses (No modification)
8. Pain and 2,00,000/- 20,000/- 20,000/-
 suffering (No modification)
 2025:KER:59088  compensation for  disfiguration 9. Compensation 5,00,000/- 1,00,800/- 1,63,800/-
 for disability [6,500/- + (6,500/- x  40 % )x 12 x 15 x  10/100]
10. Compensation Nil Nil Nil  for loss of  earning power 11. Loss of amenities 6,00,000/- 25,000/- 30,000/-
 compensation for  deformity  Total 15,18,500/- 1,75,800/- 2,43,800/-
 (limited to  10,00,000/-)

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 68,000/- (total compensation = 2,43,800/- that is, 1,75,800/- granted by the Tribunal + 68,000/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the period of 114 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to 2025:KER:59088 the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
